It depends on the clerk and how they see your being abroad, did you go together? Does it happen every year? Was it in one long trip or few over the year? Do you have good explanation for these extra days? So, no one can answer your question but to see yourself and avoid that next time.
I can tell you from my own experience, my husband was abroad more than 90 days at one year but it was because his father was sick and he left for 2 months to take care of him and then we went together for few weeks to take care for his inheritance after he passed, and we also had a 10 days trip together during holidays so all over he was away for longer than the 90 days but they didn’t care about that as there were no doubt that he lives in Israel with me
